paragraphs.text: וַיִּסַּ֤ע יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֵ֣רָה שָּׁ֑בַע וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח זְבָחִ֔ים לֵאלֹהֵ֖י אָבִ֥יו יִצְחָֽק׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el took his journey with all that he had, and came to Be'er-Sheva, and offered sacrifices unto the Elohim of his father Yitzchaq.

notes.official:
The verse stages the chapter's structural-pivot through a tightly-clustered set of literary markers. *Be'er-Sheva* (governed by the overlay `patriarchal-beer-sheva-cross-cycle-node-gen46`) is the cross-patriarchal stopping-point: Avraham planted the *eshel* there (Gen 21:33); Yitzchaq encountered the deity there with the *anokhi Elohei Avraham avikha al-tira* compound (Gen 26:23-25); Ya'aqov departed from there at the start of the Aram-period (Gen 28:10). Ya'aqov's return to the same site immediately before leaving the land is editorially-deliberate — the patriarchal-Be'er-Sheva node closes deliberately at the moment of descent.

The sacrifice *le-Elohei aviv Yitzchaq* ('unto the Elohim of his father Yitzchaq') deploys the central ancestral-god-formula `anokhi-elohei-X-avikha-ancestral-god-formula` in its third-person narrator-form. The construction names the deity through ancestral-genealogy — specifically as the deity of Yitzchaq, who had himself received the night-theophany at Be'er-Sheva at Gen 26:24. The verse therefore not only reaches back to the Avraham-Yitzchaq Be'er-Sheva tradition but specifies the Yitzchaq-tradition explicitly through the sacrifice's dedication.

The Yisra'el / Ya'aqov name-distribution begins here at v 1 with the Yisra'el-name (governed by the overlay `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-gen46`), continuing the cycle-wide pattern that the Gen 45:28 sibling-overlay inaugurated. The chapter will alternate the two names across the next four verses in editorially-significant ways.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּמַרְאֹ֣ת הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֣ב ׀ יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And Elohim spake unto Yisra'el in the visions of the night, and said, Ya'aqov, Ya'aqov. And he said, Here am I.

notes.official:
The verse deploys three structurally-load-bearing constructions in a single sentence.

**The night-vision opener.** *Be-mar'ot ha-laylah* ('in the visions of the night', governed by the overlay `mar-ot-ha-laylah-night-vision-formula-gen46`) is a fixed HB technical-term for the apocalyptic / theophanic / divinatory vision-experience. The construction's cross-corpus distribution concentrates in Daniel (the Aramaic *chezvei leiliya* at Dan 2:19, 7:7, 7:13) and Job (4:13, 33:15). The Gen 46:2 deployment is the only Genesis-internal occurrence of the specific *mar'ot ha-laylah* construction, marking the scene as belonging to the high-formality theophanic-disclosure register.

**The doubled-name call.** *Ya'aqov, Ya'aqov* (governed by the new central `doubled-name-call-theophanic-formula`) is one of the HB's most-marked theophanic stylistic-features. The cross-corpus distribution is tightly-restricted: *Avraham Avraham* at the binding (Gen 22:11); *Mosheh Mosheh* at the burning bush (Exod 3:4); *Shemu'el Shemu'el* at the prophetic-call at Shilo (1 Sam 3:10); *Ya'aqov Ya'aqov* here. The four instances are all paired with the *hineni* response (governed by the central `hineni-prophetic-response-formula`, whose appliesTo is hereby extended to v 2). The pattern signals the scene as belonging to the genre of foundational divine-call — Cassuto, Sarna, Alter, Westermann document the pattern as a deliberate theophanic stylistic-marker. The deity's choice of the older Ya'aqov-name (within the narrator's Yisra'el-frame) is editorially-marked: the moment of authorization reaches back to the patriarch's pre-Penuel identity.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֥י הָאֵ֖ל אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ אַל־תִּירָא֙ מֵרְדָ֣ה מִצְרַ֔יְמָה כִּֽי־לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֥ שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And he said, I am the El, the Elohim of thy father: fear not to go down into Mitsrayim; for I will there make of thee a great nation.

notes.official:
Verse 3 is a triple-compound divine-self-disclosure — structurally one of the densest divine-self-disclosure verses in the patriarchal narratives, paralleling Gen 26:24's four-formula compound to Yitzchaq.

**The *anokhi ha-El Elohei avikha* compound.** The verse combines (a) the *anokhi* emphatic pronoun (the canonical divine-self-disclosure opener; cf. the Decalogue's *anokhi YHWH*); (b) the *ha-El* definite-articled El-form (governed by the overlay `ha-el-divine-name-with-definite-article-gen46` — the Ya'aqov-cycle-distinctive marked-divine-name form, recurring at Gen 31:13, 35:1, 35:3; the form is distinct from the standard anarthrous El and from Elohim); (c) the *Elohei avikha* ancestral-god-formula (governed by the central `anokhi-elohei-X-avikha-ancestral-god-formula`, whose appliesTo is hereby extended to v 3).

**The *al-tira* fear-not formula.** *Al-tira me-redah Mitzraymah* ('fear not to go down into Mitsrayim') deploys the central `al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula` (whose appliesTo is hereby extended to v 3). The construction belongs to the corpus's principal divine-encouragement-formula register — Conrad 1985 documents the warrior-encouragement and patriarchal-encouragement forms; the Gen 46:3 deployment is the patriarchal-encouragement at the cycle's structural-pivot.

**The *goy gadol* great-nation promise.** *Ki le-goy gadol asimkha sham* ('for I will there make of thee a great nation') deploys the new central `goy-gadol-great-nation-promise-formula`. The construction is one of the corpus's principal patriarchal-promise-formulae, recurring at Gen 12:2 (Avraham's call), 17:20 (Yishma'el), 18:18, 21:13+18 (Hagar/Yishma'el), and reaching forward to Exod 32:10, Num 14:12, and the foundational Deut 26:5 *arami oved avi* credal-recital. The Gen 46:3 / Deut 26:5 lexical-link is one of the corpus's most-cited inner-biblical promise-and-fulfilment cross-references: the descent-promise here is named as fulfilled in the Deuteronomic recital.

paragraphs.text: אָנֹכִ֗י אֵרֵ֤ד עִמְּךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה וְאָנֹכִ֖י אַֽעַלְךָ֣ גַם־עָלֹ֑ה וְיוֹסֵ֕ף יָשִׁ֥ית יָד֖וֹ עַל־עֵינֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: I will go down with thee into Mitsrayim; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Yosef shall put his hand upon thine eyes.

notes.official:
Verse 4 is the chapter's theological centerpiece — the deity's compound descent-and-return covenant-promise — and the seed-of-the-Exodus.

**The descent-and-return compound formula.** *Anokhi ered immekha Mitzraymah ve-anokhi a'alkha gam-aloh* ('I will go down with thee into Mitsrayim; and I will also surely bring thee up again') is governed by the new central `anokhi-immekha-divine-presence-and-descent-promise-formula`. The construction combines three components: (a) the *anokhi immekha* divine-presence formula (cross-corpus Gen 26:24, 28:15, 31:3, 31:42; Exod 3:12; Deut 31:6, 8, 23; Josh 1:5, 9; Isa 41:10, etc.); (b) the descent-component *ered Mitzraymah*; (c) the paronomastic infinitive-absolute return-promise *a'alkha gam-aloh* (the *gam* + the infinitive-absolute *aloh* intensify the Hiphil *a'alkha* — 'I will most certainly bring thee up').

The construction is the seed-of-the-Exodus: Exod 3:7-8 (*ered le-hatzilo... u-le-ha'aloto*, 'I am come down to deliver... and to bring up') and Exod 6:6-8 (the four-verb covenantal-promise programmatic) verbally re-enact the Gen 46:4 promise. Cassuto reads the verse as 'the preview of the Exodus'; Westermann as the cycle's connection to the Exodus-tradition; Sternberg as 'narrative-prolepsis'; von Rad as the cycle's theological-architectonic; Childs as the lexical-thematic-source for the Exod 3-6 'bring up' programmatic.

**The close-the-eyes-at-death promise.** *Ve-Yosef yashit yado al-eineikha* ('and Yosef shall put his hand upon thine eyes') is governed by the overlay `yashit-yado-al-eineikha-close-eyes-at-death-formula-gen46`. The construction is the chapter-singular HB occurrence of the close-the-eyes-at-death formula; the gesture is a well-attested ANE death-bed ritual marking the eldest-son's duty at the moment of death. The promise resolves the chapter-internal tension: Ya'aqov can descend to Mitsrayim because Yosef will be present at the death to enact the close-family-ritual. The Gen 50:1 fulfilment (Yosef falling on his father's face, weeping, kissing) confirms the architectural-foreshadowing.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֥קָם יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִבְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־יַעֲקֹ֣ב אֲבִיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־טַפָּם֙ וְאֶת־נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם בָּעֲגָל֕וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח פַּרְעֹ֖ה לָשֵׂ֥את אֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov rose up from Be'er-Sheva: and the sons of Yisra'el carried Ya'aqov their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

notes.official:
The verse closes the chapter's opening Be'er-Sheva node and stages the wagon-transport scene.

**The wagons-cycle continuation.** The *agalot* ('wagons') of the Pharaoh-issue (Gen 45:19, 21, 27) are here put to use; the existing overlay `agalot-pharaoh-issue-wagons-yosef-cycle-gen45` is hereby extended to v 5. The wagons' arc — Pharaoh's grant (Gen 45:19) → Yosef's fulfilment (Gen 45:21) → Ya'aqov's visual-credentialing (Gen 45:27) → the transport-itself (Gen 46:5) — closes here at the chapter's structural-transition from Kena'an to Mitsrayim.

**The transport-by-class.** The verse organizes the family by class: (a) Ya'aqov-the-patriarch (carried by the sons); (b) the *taph* ('little ones' — governed by the overlay `taph-little-ones-dependents-class-yosef-cycle-gen46`, the corpus's standard dependents-class noun); (c) the wives. The able-bodied sons walk; the dependents ride. The *taph* deployment is one of the lexeme's corpus-saturating cross-corpus distribution's principal patriarchal-narrative occurrences (Gen 34:29; 43:8; 45:19; 46:5 here; 47:12; 50:8, 21); the lexeme will become a major Exodus-cycle leitwort (Exod 10:10, 24; 12:37; etc.).

**The chapter's name-shift continued.** The verse alternates Ya'aqov / Yisra'el within a single sentence: *va-yaqom Ya'aqov* (the rising-from-Be'er-Sheva: Ya'aqov-the-acting-individual); *va-yisu bnei-Yisra'el et-Ya'aqov avihem* (the carrying-by-the-collective: *bnei Yisra'el* as the covenantal-collective + Ya'aqov as the individual-father). The pattern continues the chapter-46 distribution governed by the overlay sibling-entry.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־רְכוּשָׁם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָֽכְשׁוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יְמָה יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְכָל־זַרְע֥וֹ אִתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And they took their cattle, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Kena'an, and came into Mitsrayim, Ya'aqov, and all his seed with him:

notes.official:
The verse deploys the patriarchal-mobile-wealth pair *miqneh* + *rekhush* (governed by the new overlay `miqneh-rekhush-patriarchal-mobile-wealth-formula-gen46`). The pair-formula is the corpus's standard inventory-formula for the totality of movable patriarchal possessions: livestock (*miqneh*) and accumulated goods (*rekhush*). The construction recurs at the cycle's principal patriarchal-movement scenes — Avraham's departure from Charan (Gen 12:5); Avraham-and-Lot's separation (Gen 13:6); Ya'aqov's flight from Lavan (Gen 31:18); Esav's departure to Se'ir (Gen 36:6, 7); and here at the descent to Mitsrayim.

The Gen 31:18 / Gen 46:6 lexical-link is editorially-precise: just as Ya'aqov-twenty-years-earlier-departed-from-Paddan-Aram with all his cattle and goods (Gen 31:18 *va-yinhag et-kol-miqnehu ve-et-kol-rekhusho asher rakhash... be-Paddan-Aram*), so Ya'aqov-now-departs-from-Kena'an with all his cattle and goods (Gen 46:6 *va-yiqchu et-miqneihem ve-et-rekhusham asher rakhshu be-eretz Kena'an*). The cycle-internal symmetry marks the descent-to-Mitsrayim as structurally-paralleled to all prior patriarchal-movements.

paragraphs.text: בָּנָ֞יו וּבְנֵ֤י בָנָיו֙ אִתּ֔וֹ בְּנֹתָ֛יו וּבְנ֥וֹת בָּנָ֖יו וְכָל־זַרְע֑וֹ הֵבִ֥יא אִתּ֖וֹ מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: his sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and all his seed brought he with him into Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה שְׁמ֧וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הַבָּאִ֥ים מִצְרַ֖יְמָה יַעֲקֹ֣ב וּבָנָ֑יו בְּכֹ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב רְאוּבֵֽן׃

i18n.en: And these are the names of the children of Yisra'el, who came into Mitsrayim, Ya'aqov and his sons: Re'uven, Ya'aqov's firstborn.

notes.official:
Verse 8 opens the seventy-souls genealogy — governed by the new central `seventy-souls-genealogy-archival-document-insertion-gen46`. The list is one of Genesis's three foundational archival-document insertions, alongside the Gen 5 *toledot Adam* / Sethite-line genealogy and the Gen 10 Table of Nations.

The list (vv 8-27) organizes the seventy-souls by mother — Le'ah's line (vv 8-15, 33 souls); Zilpah's line (vv 16-18, 16 souls); Rachel's line (vv 19-22, 14 souls); Bilhah's line (vv 23-25, 7 souls) — totaling 70 (33+16+14+7). The chapter's structural-architecture (the matriarchal-organization, the *eleh* + numerical-summary closures at vv 15, 18, 22, 25, the cumulative summary at vv 26-27) marks the list as a deliberately-inserted archival-document.

The cross-corpus reach extends to Exod 1:1-5 (the Exodus-narrative's abbreviated reprise, opening with the verbatim *ve-eleh shmot bnei Yisra'el* formula), Num 26 (the wilderness-census organized by tribal-eponym), and 1 Chr 2-8 (the post-exilic full-genealogy). The list-as-document is therefore not only the chapter's structural-pivot but the bridge-document between the patriarchal-narratives and the Exodus / Sinai / settlement traditions. Skinner, Westermann, Sarna, Wenham, Hamilton, Friedman document the list's source-critical character and its literary-architectural function.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֖י רְאוּבֵ֑ן חֲנ֥וֹךְ וּפַלּ֖וּא וְחֶצְר֥וֹן וְכַרְמִֽי׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Re'uven: Chanokh, and Pallu, and Chetzron, and Karmi.

notes.official: The Re'uven-line. The four sons (Chanokh, Pallu, Chetzron, Karmi) recur in the parallel-lists at Exod 6:14 (the Aharon-Mosheh genealogical-introduction) and Num 26:5-7 (the wilderness-census Re'uven-list); the chapter-internal tribal-eponyms become the Reubenite *mishpechot* (clans) at Num 26: *mishpachat ha-Chanokhi, mishpachat ha-Pallu'i, mishpachat ha-Chetzroni, mishpachat ha-Karmi*. The Chanokh-of-Re'uven here is distinct from Chanokh son of Qayin (Gen 4:17) and Chanokh son of Yered (Gen 5:18); the Chetzron-of-Re'uven here is distinct from Chetzron son of Peretz at v 12 (though both belong to the same generation through different fathers). 1 Chr 5:3 preserves the same four-son tradition into the post-exilic period.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֗וֹן יְמוּאֵ֧ל וְיָמִ֛ין וְאֹ֖הַד וְיָכִ֣ין וְצֹ֑חַר וְשָׁא֖וּל בֶּן־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽית׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Shim'on: Yemu'el, and Yamin, and Ohad, and Yakhin, and Tzochar, and Sha'ul the son of a Kena'anite woman.

notes.official:
The Shim'on-line closes with a unique mother-ethnicity-qualifier: *Sha'ul ben ha-Kena'anit* ('Sha'ul the son of a Kena'anite woman' — governed by the new overlay `ben-ha-kenaanit-shimon-canaanitess-son-gen46`). The qualifier is the seventy-souls list's ONLY mother-ethnicity-marker; among the four matriarchal-lines and their descendants, only Sha'ul is given an explicit mother-ethnicity identification. The cross-corpus verbatim-parallel at Exod 6:15 (*Sha'ul ben ha-Kena'anit, eleh mishpechot Shim'on*) confirms the qualifier as a fixed-tradition element of the Shim'on-line; the Num 26:13 wilderness-census omits it.

Modern critical scholarship reads the qualifier through several frames: documentary-historical (preserving an older inter-ethnic marriage tradition); source-critical (a fossilization in the Gen 46 / Exod 6 tradition that the Num 26 tradition omits); literary-narrative (possibly foreshadowing Shim'on's later tribal-fate as the smallest and most-dispersed tribe, omitted from Mosheh's Deut 33 blessing and enclaved within Yehudah at Josh 19:1-9). The qualifier's interpretive readings are documented in commentary; no single reading is adjudicated.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֖י לֵוִ֑י גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן קְהָ֖ת וּמְרָרִֽי׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Qehat, and Merari.

notes.official: The Levi-line. The three sons (Gershon, Qehat, Merari) become the three foundational Levitical-clans: the Gershonites, the Qehatites, and the Merarites — the threefold Levitical-class-division that structures the Mishkan-transport instructions (Num 3-4), the Levitical settlements (Num 26:57-58; Josh 21), and the post-exilic Levitical-genealogies (1 Chr 6, 23). The verse names the Levitical-tribal-foundation that will become foundational to the priestly-cultic establishment from the Mosaic period forward.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה עֵ֧ר וְאוֹנָ֛ן וְשֵׁלָ֖ה וָפֶ֣רֶץ וָזָ֑רַח וַיָּ֨מָת עֵ֤ר וְאוֹנָן֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ חֶצְר֥וֹן וְחָמֽוּל׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Yehudah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Peretz, and Zerach; but Er and Onan died in the land of Kena'an. And the sons of Peretz were Chetzron and Chamul.

notes.official:
The Yehudah-line contains the seventy-souls list's ONLY narrative-historical aside: *va-yamot Er ve-Onan be-eretz Kena'an* ('but Er and Onan died in the land of Kena'an' — governed by the new overlay `er-onan-died-in-kenaan-gen38-back-reference-gen46`, with bidirectional sibling-link to the existing overlay `ve-shichet-artzah-onan-euphemism` at Gen 38:9). The aside is editorially-marked: among the seventy-souls list's 19 verses, only the Yehudah-line includes this kind of explanatory-narrative note on prior-deaths. The cross-reference is to Gen 38:7-10 — Er was put-to-death by YHWH for being *ra* in YHWH's eyes; Onan was put-to-death by YHWH for the *shichet artzah* act (governed by the Gen 38 sibling-overlay).

The Peretz-grandsons (Chetzron and Chamul) are explicitly named, making the Yehudah-line one of only two lines in the genealogy with explicit-grandson-naming (the Asher-line at v 17 also names grandsons). The Peretz-line is the Davidic-line's foundation: Peretz is David's tenth-generation ancestor (Ruth 4:18-22, the *toledot Peretz*; 1 Chr 2:4-15). The genealogy's editorial-architecture therefore not only cross-references Gen 38 but foregrounds the line that will become the royal-Davidic line.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֖י יִשָׂשכָ֑ר תּוֹלָ֥ע וּפֻוָּ֖ה וְי֥וֹב וְשִׁמְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Yissakhar: Tola, and Puvvah, and Yov, and Shimron.

notes.official:
The Yissakhar-line contains a documented textual-critical variant at the third son's name: MT reads *Yov* (יוֹב); the Samaritan Pentateuch, the LXX, the Num 26:24 wilderness-census-parallel, and the 1 Chr 7:1 post-exilic-list all read *Yashuv* (יָשׁוּב — governed by the new overlay `yov-yashuv-ketiv-qere-yissachar-textual-variant-gen46`). The MT-tradition stands alone in preserving *Yov*; the broader textual-tradition preserves *Yashuv*.

The variant is widely understood as a transmission-error in the MT (the omission of the *shin* in transcription, or a graphical-corruption). KJV/ASV preserve the MT reading and Anglicize as 'Job' — which is unrelated to the famously-suffering Iyov (אִיּוֹב) of the wisdom-tradition; the names are distinct in Hebrew. NJPS and NRSV follow the cross-corpus *Yashuv* reading. The MT-fidelity baseline established at Gen 22:13 (the *ayil* / *achar echad* variant) is followed here: MT *Yov* preserved with WoH transliteration; the *Yashuv* textual-tradition documented in commentary. Tov treats the variant as a Vorlage / transmission case in the standard textual-critical apparatus.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֖י זְבוּלֻ֑ן סֶ֥רֶד וְאֵל֖וֹן וְיַחְלְאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Zevulun: Sered, and Elon, and Yachle'el.

notes.official: The Zevulun-line. The three sons recur as the Zevulunite *mishpechot* at Num 26:26 (the Sardites, the Elonites, the Yachle'elites).

paragraphs.text: אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָֽלְדָ֤ה לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת דִּינָ֣ה בִתּ֑וֹ כָּל־נֶ֧פֶשׁ בָּנָ֛יו וּבְנוֹתָ֖יו שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֹֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Le'ah, whom she bare unto Ya'aqov in Paddan-Aram, with his daughter Dinah: all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty and three.

notes.official:
The Le'ah-line closure: *eleh bnei Le'ah asher yaldah le-Ya'aqov be-Paddan-Aram ve-et Dinah vito* ('these are the sons of Le'ah, whom she bare unto Ya'aqov in Paddan-Aram, with his daughter Dinah'); the sub-total is 33 (the six sons + Re'uven's 4 + Shim'on's 6 + Levi's 3 + Yehudah's 5 [minus Er and Onan dead] + Yehudah's 2 grandsons + Yissakhar's 4 + Zevulun's 3 + Dinah). The existing overlay `paddan-aram-binyamin-contradiction-documentary-seam` (anchored at Gen 35:26) is hereby extended to v 15: the same *be-Paddan-Aram* formula construction recurs here, and the broader source-critical observation about the P-source's claim that the sons were born in Paddan-Aram extends to this chapter.

Note that v 15 itself does NOT directly surface the Binyamin-contradiction: Le'ah's sons WERE all born in Paddan-Aram, so the *be-Paddan-Aram* formula is correct for Le'ah's line specifically. The contradiction with the Gen 35:16-18 Binyamin-birth-narrative does not appear here directly; Dinah is named here as Ya'aqov's daughter and is consistently a Paddan-Aram birth. The appliesTo extension is therefore scope-formalization of the broader observation rather than a direct documentary-seam at v 15 itself.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֣י גָ֔ד צִפְי֥וֹן וְחַגִּ֖י שׁוּנִ֣י וְאֶצְבֹּ֑ן עֵרִ֥י וַֽאֲרוֹדִ֖י וְאַרְאֵלִֽי׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Gad: Tziphyon, and Chaggi, Shuni, and Etzbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.

notes.official: The Gad-line. The seven sons recur as the Gadite *mishpechot* at Num 26:15-18 with some name-form variations (Tziphyon / Tzephon; Etzbon / Ozni; Arodi / Arod). The variations are typical of the genealogy's name-form-variation pattern across the parallel-lists; the variants are documented in standard textual-critical commentary (Skinner, Hamilton, Speiser) without bearing on translation-decisions.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֗ר יִמְנָ֧ה וְיִשְׁוָ֛ה וְיִשְׁוִ֥י וּבְרִיעָ֖ה וְשֶׂ֣רַח אֲחֹתָ֑ם וּבְנֵ֣י בְרִיעָ֔ה חֶ֖בֶר וּמַלְכִּיאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Asher: Yimnah, and Yishvah, and Yishvi, and Beriah, and Serach their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Chever, and Malki'el.

notes.official:
The Asher-line names *Serach achotam* ('Serach their sister' — governed by the new overlay `serach-bat-asher-only-named-granddaughter-gen46`). Serach is one of only two women named in the entire seventy-souls genealogy; the other is Dinah at v 15. Both are explicit grand-daughters in the genealogical-architecture, and only Le'ah's-line (Dinah) and Asher's-line (Serach) name granddaughters. The cross-corpus attestations at Num 26:46 (*ve-shem bat-Asher Serach*) and 1 Chr 7:30 (verbatim-identical to Gen 46:17) preserve the tradition into the wilderness-period and the post-exilic period respectively.

The rabbinic-aggadic tradition develops an extensive Serach-corpus: Targum Pseudo-Jonathan, Genesis Rabbah 94:9, b. Sotah 13a, and Sefer Ha-Yashar record traditions that Serach was exceptionally long-lived (surviving from the seventy-souls-descent to Mitsrayim through to the Exodus and beyond), that she was the one who informed Mosheh of the location of Yosef's bones (cf. Exod 13:19), and that she was 'taken alive into the Garden of Eden' alongside Eliyahu. The named-female-grandchild Asher-tradition is one of the genealogy's most extensively-developed aggadic-traditions; the rationale documents the tradition without adjudication.

The verse also names Beriah's two sons (Chever and Malki'el), making the Asher-line one of only two lines with explicit-grandson-naming (the Yehudah-Peretz-line at v 12 being the other).

paragraphs.text: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י זִלְפָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָבָ֖ן לְלֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֤לֶד אֶת־אֵ֙לֶּה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה נָֽפֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Lavan gave to Le'ah his daughter; and these she bare unto Ya'aqov, even sixteen souls.

notes.official: The Zilpah-line closure: the handmaid-of-Le'ah's-line (Gad + Asher) totals 16 souls.

paragraphs.text: בְּנֵ֤י רָחֵל֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יוֹסֵ֖ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃

i18n.en: The sons of Rachel Ya'aqov's wife: Yosef and Binyamin.

notes.official: The Rachel-line opener with the editorially-marked epithet *eshet Ya'aqov* ('Ya'aqov's wife'). The epithet — applied to Rachel and not to Le'ah, Zilpah, or Bilhah — is consistent with the cycle's Rachel-centric narrative-marking (cf. Gen 44:27 Ya'aqov's marked *shenayim yaledah-li ishti*, 'my wife bare me two sons', governed by the existing overlay `shenayim-yaledah-li-ishti-rachel-exclusive-wife-gen44'). The Rachel-line stands grammatically as the favored-line in the genealogy: Le'ah's sons and the handmaids' sons are introduced by *eleh bnei X* without spousal-epithet; Rachel alone is *eshet Ya'aqov*.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּוָּלֵ֣ד לְיוֹסֵף֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֣ן אֹ֑ן אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And unto Yosef in the land of Mitsrayim were born Menasheh and Ephraim, whom Asnat the daughter of Poti-Phera priest of On bare unto him.

notes.official:
Verse 20 contains the chapter's most-cited LXX/MT textual variant. The MT lists only Menasheh and Ephraim as Yosef's two Mitsrayim-born sons; the LXX-tradition expands the verse with five additional descendants — Menasheh's son Makhir and grandson Galaad; Ephraim's sons Sutalaam and Taam; Sutalaam's son Edom — drawn from the Num 26:29, 35 parallel-tradition (governed by the new overlay `lxx-mt-seventy-five-vs-seventy-yosef-line-variant-gen46`, with bidirectional central-sibling-link to `shivim-nefesh-seventy-souls-foundational-number-LXX-variant`). The LXX expansion produces the cumulative seventy-FIVE count at v 27, against the MT seventy.

The 4QExoda Qumran-fragment reads seventy-five at the Exod 1:5 parallel, confirming the seventy-five count's Hebrew-Vorlage attestation. The LXX-tradition reading is the basis of the Acts 7:14 NT-tradition (Stephen's speech: *en psychais hebdomekonta pente* — 'threescore and fifteen souls'). The variant is one of the most-cited HB textual-critical-cruxes (Tov *Textual Criticism* 2012; Wevers *Notes on the Greek Text of Genesis* 1993; Fitzmyer *AB Acts* 1998 on the Acts 7:14 reading). The Editor's approach: translate the MT as the surface-baseline; document the LXX expansion in commentary; no theological-typological adjudication.

The verse also deploys the Egyptological names governed by the existing central entries: *Poti-Phera* (`poti-phera-egyptian-name-priest-of-on`); *On* (`on-heliopolis-egyptian-toponym`, the Hellenistic Heliopolis); *Asnat* (the wife). The Menasheh and Ephraim aetiologies (governed by the existing central entries) recur from Gen 41:51-52.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֗ן בֶּ֤לַע וָבֶ֙כֶר֙ וְאַשְׁבֵּ֔ל גֵּרָ֥א וְנַעֲמָ֖ן אֵחִ֣י וָרֹ֑אשׁ מֻפִּ֥ים וְחֻפִּ֖ים וָאָֽרְדְּ׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Binyamin: Bela, and Bekher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Na'aman, Echi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Chuppim, and Ard.

notes.official:
Verse 21 is one of the most-cited HB genealogical-textual-critical-cruxes. Binyamin's ten-son list here (Bela, Bekher, Ashbel, Gera, Na'aman, Echi, Rosh, Muppim, Chuppim, Ard) diverges substantially from the three principal parallel-lists (governed by the new overlay `binyamin-sons-list-textual-crux-gen46`):

- **Num 26:38-40** lists FIVE sons (Bela, Ashbel, Achiram, Shfufam, Chufam) plus two Bela-sons (Ard and Na'aman) — i.e., names that appear here as Binyamin's sons are reclassified as Binyamin's grandsons-through-Bela.
- **1 Chr 7:6** lists THREE sons (Bela, Bekher, Yedi'a'el).
- **1 Chr 8:1-2** lists FIVE sons (Bela, Ashbel, Achrach, Nochah, Rafa).

The variations include: (a) the total count (10 / 5 / 3 / 5); (b) name-form variants (Echi / Achiram; Muppim / Shfufam; Chuppim / Chufam — possibly metathesis-and-corruption variants of the same names); (c) the generation-confusion (Ard, Na'aman, and Gera as Binyamin's sons here but as Bela's sons in Num 26:40); (d) the *Rosh* singular-attestation (no parallel in any other list; sometimes proposed as a scribal-corruption, sometimes preserved as a genuine name).

Two main interpretive readings are documented even-handedly without adjudication: the **documentary-critical reading** (Wellhausen, Skinner, Friedman: the variations reflect different source-traditions and document the historical-tradition's flux) and the **harmonizing reading** (Cassuto, Hamilton: the variations can be reconciled through generation-shifting across Davidic-Solomonic-period census-revisions). Sarna preserves both readings without adjudicating. The MT is translated as-is with WoH proper-name transliteration.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּ֖ד לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב כָּל־נֶ֖פֶשׁ אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Ya'aqov: all the souls were fourteen.

notes.official: The Rachel-line closure. The MT-tradition's count of 14 (Yosef + 2 sons + Binyamin + 10 sons) is the sub-total in the seventy-souls arithmetic. The LXX-tradition's expanded count would push the Rachel-line higher and produce the cumulative seventy-five (see the v 20 commentary and the overlay sibling-link to the central seventy-souls entry).

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵי־דָ֖ן חֻשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Dan: Chushim.

notes.official: The Dan-line names a single entity in a plural-form: *Chushim* (חֻשִׁים; governed by the new overlay `chushim-bne-dan-plural-clan-form-gen46`). The construction *u-vnei-Dan Chushim* with the plural-construct *bnei* + the plural-form-name admits three principal readings: (a) the clan-name-plural reading (a single eponymous-son whose name has a plural-form-ending — comparable to *Mitsrayim* and *Yerushalayim* as dual-form names of single entities); (b) the multiple-sons-collective reading; (c) the textual-corruption reading. The Num 26:42 wilderness-census Dan-list reads *Shucham* (a metathesis-variant of *Chusham/Chushim*); the variant is flagged in commentary without adjudication.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֖י נַפְתָּלִ֑י יַחְצְאֵ֥ל וְגוּנִ֖י וְיֵ֥צֶר וְשִׁלֵּֽם׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Naftali: Yachtze'el, and Guni, and Yetzer, and Shillem.

notes.official: The Naftali-line. The four sons recur as the Naftalite *mishpechot* at Num 26:48-49 with the name-form variant *Yachtze'el* / *Yachtz'el*; the lists are otherwise stable across the parallel-traditions.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִלְהָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָבָ֖ן לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֧לֶד אֶת־אֵ֛לֶּה לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ שִׁבְעָֽה׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Lavan gave unto Rachel his daughter, and these she bare unto Ya'aqov: all the souls were seven.

notes.official: The Bilhah-line closure: the handmaid-of-Rachel's-line (Dan + Naftali) totals 7 souls.

paragraphs.text: כָּל־הַ֠נֶּפֶשׁ הַבָּאָ֨ה לְיַעֲקֹ֤ב מִצְרַ֙יְמָה֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י יְרֵכ֔וֹ מִלְּבַ֖ד נְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵי־יַעֲקֹ֑ב כָּל־נֶ֖פֶשׁ שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵֽׁשׁ׃

i18n.en: All the souls that came with Ya'aqov into Mitsrayim, that came out of his loins, besides Ya'aqov's sons' wives, all the souls were threescore and six;

notes.official:
Verse 26 closes the chapter's first summary-count at 66 souls. The construction *yotz'ei yerekho* ('that came out of his loins' — governed by the new overlay `yotzei-yerekho-loins-procession-euphemism-gen46`) is the corpus's standard direct-male-line-descent euphemism. The *yerekh* ('thigh') is the standard ANE-cultural euphemism for the male-reproductive-organs; the *yotz'ei yerekh* ('goers-out of the thigh') construction names the people-who-proceed-from-the-male-line.

The cross-corpus distribution: Gen 35:11 (the El-Shaddai promise: *u-melakhim me-chalatzeikha yetze'u*, using the parallel-euphemism *chalatzayim* 'loins'); Exod 1:5 (the verbatim-construction *yotz'ei yerekh-Ya'aqov shiv'im nafesh*, directly cross-referencing this verse); Judg 8:30 (Gid'on's seventy sons *yotz'ei yerekho*); 1 Kgs 8:19 / 2 Chr 6:9 (the Davidic-covenant fulfilment formulation). The Gen 46:26 / Exod 1:5 lexical-link is one of the corpus's most-cited inner-biblical genealogical-cross-references.

The arithmetic: 66 = 70 minus Yosef + Menasheh + Ephraim + Ya'aqov himself; the v 27 cumulative count adds these four back to reach 70 (MT) or 75 (LXX). The ASV's 'loins' modesty-flattens the literal 'thigh'; both renderings are documented.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֛ף אֲשֶׁר־יֻלַּד־ל֥וֹ בְמִצְרַ֖יִם נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֑יִם כָּל־הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ לְבֵֽית־יַעֲקֹ֛ב הַבָּ֥אָה מִצְרַ֖יְמָה שִׁבְעִֽים׃ (פ)

i18n.en: and the sons of Yosef, who were born to him in Mitsrayim, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Ya'aqov, that came into Mitsrayim, were threescore and ten.

notes.official:
Verse 27 closes the genealogy with the foundational seventy-souls count (governed by the new central `shivim-nefesh-seventy-souls-foundational-number-LXX-variant`). The MT cumulative count is 70 (66 + 2 [Menasheh and Ephraim] + Yosef + Ya'aqov = 70). The LXX cumulative count is 75 (reflecting the v 20 expansion's five additional Yosef-line descendants).

The seventy-souls count is one of the HB's most-load-bearing foundational-numbers: cross-corpus to Exod 1:5 (the Exodus-narrative's abbreviated reprise) and Deut 10:22 (the Deuteronomic-credal-recital: *be-shiv'im nefesh yardu avoteikha Mitzraymah, ve-attah samkha YHWH Elohekha ke-khokhvei ha-shamayim la-rov* — 'thy fathers went down into Mitsrayim with threescore and ten persons; and now YHWH thy Elohim hath made thee as the stars of heaven for multitude'). The Gen 46:27 / Exod 1:5 / Deut 10:22 cluster is the corpus's foundational descent-and-growth narrative-architecture.

The wider seventy-typology cross-corpus distribution is documented WITHOUT theological-typological adjudication: the seventy elders of Israel (Exod 24:1, 9; Num 11:16, 24-25); the seventy years of Babylonian exile (Jer 25:11-12, 29:10; Dan 9:2); the seventy-week-prophecy (Dan 9:24-27); the ANE-comparative seventy sons of El at Ugarit (KTU 1.4 VI 46). No Sanhedrin-typology is asserted; no 70-nations-of-Gen-10 typology is asserted; no NT-elders-typology is adjudicated.

The Acts 7:14 NT-tradition reading (Stephen's *en psychais hebdomekonta pente*, 'threescore and fifteen souls') follows the LXX-tradition; the textual-critical implication that Stephen was working from the LXX-Vorlage rather than from the MT is documented as named-scholarship apparatus.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־יְהוּדָ֞ה שָׁלַ֤ח לְפָנָיו֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף לְהוֹרֹ֥ת לְפָנָ֖יו גֹּ֑שְׁנָה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אַ֥רְצָה גֹּֽשֶׁן׃

i18n.en: And he sent Yehudah before him unto Yosef, to show the way before him unto Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.

notes.official:
Yehudah — not Re'uven (the firstborn), not Yosef-already-in-Mitsrayim — is sent before Ya'aqov to Yosef. The choice is editorially-marked and continues the cycle-wide Yehudah-as-leader emergence pattern (governed by the new overlay `yehudah-sent-before-leadership-pattern-gen46`). The pattern is observable from Gen 37:26-27 (the sale-speech, Yehudah's first-recorded leadership moment); through Gen 38 (the Yehudah-Tamar narrative as a complete tribal-line foundation); Gen 43:3-10 (the surety-pledge negotiation, the *arav-eravon* pledge governed by the existing overlay); Gen 44:14-34 (the great substitution-speech, the cycle's longest single-speech); to Gen 46:28 (here, the sent-before-Ya'aqov mission). The pattern reaches forward to Gen 49:8-12 (the lion-of-Yehudah patriarchal blessing) and beyond to the Davidic-monarchic and Messianic traditions.

The verb *le-horot* (Hiphil infinitive of *yarah* III, 'to teach, instruct, direct, guide') here deploys the directional-guidance sense: Yehudah is to *direct the way* before Ya'aqov to Goshen. The Hiphil of *yarah* is the standard stem of the *torah*-root family; its broader cross-corpus reach into the law-teaching register (Exod 24:12; Deut; the *torah* / *moreh* / *horah* cluster) is reserved for major central treatment when those texts are translated. The Gen 46:28 deployment is in the topographical-guide register; the law-teaching sense is documented in commentary.

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּאְסֹ֤ר יוֹסֵף֙ מֶרְכַּבְתּ֔וֹ וַיַּ֛עַל לִקְרַֽאת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אָבִ֖יו גֹּ֑שְׁנָה וַיֵּרָ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וַיִּפֹּל֙ עַל־צַוָּארָ֔יו וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ עַל־צַוָּארָ֖יו עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: And Yosef made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yisra'el his father, to Goshen; and he presented himself unto him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

notes.official:
The reunion-climax. *Va-yera elav* ('and he presented himself unto him' / literally 'and he showed/appeared himself unto him' — governed by the new overlay `va-yera-elav-reunion-as-theophany-lexical-echo-gen46`) deploys the Niphal of *ra'ah* in verbatim-coincidence with the standard HB theophanic-formula. The construction *va-yera + (preposition) + X* with the deity as implied-subject opens the patriarchal-and-Mosaic theophany-scenes (Gen 12:7 to Avram; Gen 17:1 to Avraham at El-Shaddai; Gen 18:1 the three-visitors; Gen 26:2 + 26:24 to Yitzchaq; Gen 35:1 + 35:9 to Ya'aqov; Exod 6:3 the P-source's foundational divine-name verse). The Gen 46:29 deployment applies the same construction to the human-to-human Yosef-Ya'aqov reunion.

The literary-architectural force is named in mainstream scholarship (Sarna, Alter, Cassuto, Westermann): the chapter is structurally-bracketed by theophanic-language. The chapter opens with a literal-theophany at Be'er-Sheva (vv 1-4); the chapter's reunion-climax at v 29 uses the same lexical-register to mark the son-father reunion as the human-theophanic correlative of the divine-theophanic-opening. The ASV's 'presented himself unto him' preserves the reunion-register reading without surfacing the theophanic-lexical-echo; the literal 'appeared to him' would surface the echo at the cost of the reunion-narrative naturalness.

The *va-yippol al-tzavarav va-yevk* construction is the third member of the Genesis-internal reunion-embrace-and-weeping formula cluster (governed by the existing overlay `va-yippol-al-tzavarav-reunion-embrace-formula-gen45`, whose appliesTo is hereby extended to v 29). The cluster: Gen 33:4 (Esav-Ya'aqov, with the puncta extraordinaria over the kiss-verb); Gen 45:14-15 (Yosef-Binyamin and Yosef-brothers); Gen 46:29 (Yosef-Ya'aqov here). The triple-cluster is the cycle's signature reunion-formula architecture. The doubled *al-tzavarav od* ('on his neck a good while') intensifies the weeping-duration, marking this as the cycle's most-extended weeping-scene.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף אָמ֣וּתָה הַפָּ֑עַם אַחֲרֵי֙ רְאוֹתִ֣י אֶת־פָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י עוֹדְךָ֖ חָֽי׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el said unto Yosef, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, that thou art yet alive.

notes.official:
Ya'aqov's death-readiness statement *amutah ha-pa'am* ('now let me die' — governed by the new overlay `amutah-ha-paam-death-readiness-yaaqov-gen46`) closes the cycle's Gen 45:28 → 46:30 death-readiness arc. The construction combines the cohortative *amutah* (Qal volitive of *mut* 'to die') with the emphatic *ha-pa'am* ('this time / this very moment').

The arc: at Gen 45:28 Ya'aqov resolved to go-and-see-the-son-before-dying (*elkhah ve-er'ennu be-terem amut*, 'I will go and see him before I die' — the future-oriented resolve); at Gen 46:30 Ya'aqov declares the chapter's-purpose-completed and his readiness to die now (*amutah ha-pa'am acharei re'oti et-paneikha*, 'now let me die, since I have seen thy face' — the present-readiness oriented toward a past-completed seeing). The arc traces resolve → going → seeing → readiness.

The sibling-link to the existing overlay `va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45` (Gen 45:27) is bidirectional. The two entries jointly track the cycle's affective-pivots across the chapter-transition: Gen 45:26 fainting-of-the-heart → Gen 45:27 spirit-revival → Gen 45:28 resolve-to-see → Gen 46:30 readiness-to-die. The chapter-46 verse closes the cycle's emotional arc that began at Gen 37:34 with the *tarof toraf* grief-rending — twenty-two years of mourning resolved here at the reunion. The Yisra'el-name (rather than Ya'aqov) marks the patriarch as in the covenantal-determined register at the moment of stating the resolution.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ וְאֶל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו אֶעֱלֶ֖ה וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאֹֽמְרָ֣ה אֵלָ֔יו אַחַ֧י וּבֵית־אָבִ֛י אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־כְּנַ֖עַן בָּ֥אוּ אֵלָֽי׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto his brethren, and unto his father's house, I will go up, and tell Pharaoh, and will say unto him, My brethren, and my father's house, who were in the land of Kena'an, are come unto me;

notes.official: Yosef's Pharaoh-audience preparation begins. The construction *e'eleh ve-aggidah le-Far'oh* ('I will go up, and tell Pharaoh') deploys the standard up-to-the-court verb *alah* (Hiphil here in v 4 of the deity, Qal here of Yosef); Yosef's narrative-control of the audience anticipates the Gen 47:1-12 royal-presentation scene.

paragraphs.text: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֙ רֹ֣עֵי צֹ֔אן כִּֽי־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה הָי֑וּ וְצֹאנָ֧ם וּבְקָרָ֛ם וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם הֵבִֽיאוּ׃

i18n.en: and the men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.

notes.official: Yosef's audience-preparation continues with the occupational-class identification: *anshei miqneh* ('men of cattle / keepers of cattle'). The construction uses the same *miqneh* lexeme that the v 6 mobile-wealth-pair deploys, here in the occupational-class-marker register (*anshei miqneh* = pastoral herders). The preparation foregrounds the brothers' occupational-class for the Pharaoh-audience, anticipating the v 34 strategic deployment around the *to'evah*-marker.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֕ה כִּֽי־יִקְרָ֥א לָכֶ֖ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַ֖ר מַה־מַּעֲשֵׂיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What is your occupation?

paragraphs.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִקְנֶ֜ה הָי֤וּ עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ מִנְּעוּרֵ֣ינוּ וְעַד־עַ֔תָּה גַּם־אֲנַ֖חְנוּ גַּם־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ בַּעֲב֗וּר תֵּשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן כִּֽי־תוֹעֲבַ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם כָּל־רֹ֥עֵה צֹֽאן׃

i18n.en: that ye shall say, Thy servants have been keepers of cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Mitsrim.

notes.official:
Yosef's audience-strategy closes with the explicit deployment of the central `toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword` (whose appliesTo is hereby extended to v 34, formalizing what the entry's existing rationale already names). The verse is the chapter's second deployment of the *to'evah*-marker in the cycle (after Gen 43:32, where the food-segregation was named as *to'evah le-Mitzrayim*); the chapter-internal pair therefore covers the Egyptian-evaluator *to'evah* on the dietary axis (Gen 43:32) and on the occupational axis (Gen 46:34).

The shepherds-as-*to'evah* observation is editorially-loaded. Modern scholarship cross-references the note to the **Hyksos-memory**: the Asiatic shepherd-kings who ruled Egypt in the Second Intermediate Period (c. 1650-1550 BCE) and against whom the post-Hyksos Egyptian polemic was directed. Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* (1959), Redford *Egypt, Canaan, and Israel* (1992), Bietak *Avaris and Piramesse* on Tell ed-Dab'a, and Hoffmeier *Israel in Egypt* (1996) document the Hyksos-period historical-context and the post-Hyksos Egyptian anti-shepherd-foreigner polemic. The documentary-critical reading treats the *to'evah*-note as an editorial-explanation of the Israelites' segregation in Goshen; the cross-cultural-historical reading treats it as preserving authentic Egyptian-cultural-memory of the Hyksos-rule period. Both readings are documented without adjudication.

The verse's strategic-rhetoric: Yosef instructs the brothers to identify as *anshei miqneh* ('keepers of cattle') precisely BECAUSE the shepherd-occupation is *to'evat Mitzrayim* — the very segregation-marker that makes them unwelcome in the Egyptian-court is what makes Goshen-settlement available. The brothers' acceptable distance is engineered through their visible occupational-class. No WoH synthesis on the segregation; the rhetoric is documented as named-scholarship literary observation.
